newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.100 cent a lb lower to 0.100 higher while pork belly futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts anticipate carryover long liquidation following the weak undertone to cash pork prices. Demand for pork is seen light ahead of the holiday which should weigh on cash prices early next week. Technicals also turned lower Thursday, they said.
However, others cited the steady to firm tone to cash hog markets Friday morning.

Packers are showing better-than-expected demand for hogs to meet a possible larger Saturday kill. They likely want to boost kills ahead of the short slaughter week next week, especially with profit margins still in the black, they said.

Pork bellies were expected to be weighed down by technical pressure with an easier tone to cash bellies adding to pressure. Bacon shows a seasonally weak period during the holidays when consumer attention turns to more traditional meats, they said.
Chartists are looking for a 50 percent correction from the recent runup in prices.

Evening of positions may develop ahead of Friday afternoon's USDA monthly Cold Storage Report. The report is expected to show frozen pork belly stocks at historically low levels for this time of year, analysts added.
The average analyst estimate for the report was 16.0 million lbs in storage on November 1 which compares with the average for the last 10 years of 22.8 million lbs.
